title: What is Magical Realism?
use_cases: Use when distinguishing between high fantasy world-building and real-world magical elements
Implement when writing stories where characters accept impossible events as mundane occurrences
Configure when integrating symbolic or metaphorical magic into a contemporary grounded setting
Use when exploring the difference between learned magic systems and inherent surreal reality
content:
Now, let’s look at the other side. What is magical realism? This genre is trickier. It is more subtle. The name gives you a big clue. It is a mix of the magical and the real.

Here are the main characteristics of magical realism. First, the story is set in our world. It is not a separate, made-up place. It happens in a real-world setting. It could be a small town in South America. It could be a city in Japan. It could be a house in your neighborhood. It feels solid and normal.

But then, something impossible happens. A woman might float into the air. A ghost might sit down for dinner. A river might flow with blood for a day. Here is the most important part. Nobody in the story thinks this is weird. The characters accept the magical event as a normal part of life. They do not stop and say, “Wow, magic!” They just… deal with it. The author writes about the magical event in a very normal, matter-of-fact tone. This blending reality and fantasy is the core of the genre.

In magical realism, the magic is not a system. No one learns it. There are no spellbooks. It is just part of the world, like the weather. It is surreal vs supernatural. Fantasy is supernatural. It is “above” our nature. Magical realism is surreal. It is “part of” our reality, just a strange part. The magic often has a deeper meaning. It might be a symbol. It might be a way to talk about history, or pain, or love. It uses symbolic reality to make a point about our real world.

So, let’s put them side by side. This is the main event. The fantasy fiction vs magical realism debate comes down to a few big differences. We can break them down to make it easy.
